stories.title: Baseline (as is)
stories.what_happened: Nothing has gone wrong yet. This is the plan for the coming year, before any disruption.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It serves 99.50% of demand at a landed cost of €20.33M, moving it in 2,419 truck trips. It clears every governance gate, so it could be released to the factory without anyone signing it off.

stories.title: A supplier goes dark
stories.what_happened: The flavour house that supplies Lemon Flavour Concentrate shuts for 13 weeks, from day 7 to day 98.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It saw the shutdown coming and bought 6,965 L of lemon flavour concentrate in the week before it (it would normally buy 0 L), bought 0 L while the vendor was shut, and carried on afterwards. Service held at 99.50%.

stories.title: A road closes
stories.what_happened: The road from Breda Bottling to DC Tilburg closes for two weeks, from day 7 to day 21.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It filled DC Tilburg up before the road closed — 24 trucks in the first week, against 5 normally — sent 0 while it was shut, and rebuilt stock afterwards with 62 trucks in the following three weeks, against 34. Service held at 99.50%.

stories.title: A key account's promotion order
stories.what_happened: Noordster Supermarkten, the highest-priority account, places a promotion order for an extra 125k cases of Sparkling Lemonade, due on day 10.
stories.what_the_plan_did: Noordster Supermarkten were filled at 100.0%. Where capacity ran out, lower-priority accounts went short first: Zuinig & Zo (priority 40) short 4 more cases; Groothandel Molenzicht (priority 60) short 246 more cases.

stories.title: Electrify two lanes
stories.what_happened: Breda Bottling's own trucks to DC Tilburg and DC Rotterdam switch to battery-electric tractors (CO2 class 5), which pay a fraction of the Dutch truck toll.
stories.what_the_plan_did: The toll on those two lanes falls from €9,276 to €1,803 over the year, and the plan's whole toll from €18k to €11k. Transport emissions by the ISO 14083 method go from 213 to 129 tonnes CO2e. The trucks' own cost is not modelled, so the toll saving is the most this decision could save, not its business case, and the electric emission factor is illustrative.

stories.title: A tariff on imported concentrate
stories.what_happened: From day 49 to the end of the year, an extra 25% import duty applies to Lemon Flavour Concentrate, which the bottling plant buys from the United States, on top of the EU's ordinary 12.8% duty.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It bought 19k L before the duty started, against 4,000 L in the baseline, so almost no concentrate pays the duty (purchases unchanged). On the baseline the duty would have cost €51k. Carrying the stock is not free, but the landed cost change (+€1,822) is inside the €114k the plans are solved to, so this run cannot say how much of the duty buying ahead really saves. Service is 99.50%. The concentrate has no shelf life or storage limit in this demo; a real tariff study would check both, and price another source of supply.

stories.title: The new product takes off
stories.what_happened: Noordster Supermarkten lists Sparkling Lemonade Zero, launched in April, in every store for the summer, and orders 100k cases for mid-May to mid-July. Its forecast rests on 38 weeks of history.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It makes 87k more cases of Sparkling Lemonade Zero over the year. Co-packing does not change (11k cases), and Sparkling Lemonade, which shares the bottling lines, is not touched. Where capacity ran out, lower-priority accounts went short first: Groothandel Molenzicht (priority 60) short 918 more cases. Service is 99.51%.

stories.title: A bottling line goes down in summer
stories.what_happened: Breda Bottling's Sparkling Lemonade filling line is out for four weeks, mid-June to mid-July, for a rebuild after a breakdown. The date is known in advance.
stories.what_the_plan_did: Before the line goes down, it builds Sparkling Lemonade ahead at Oss Foods rather than Breda Bottling: Oss Foods makes 381k more cases and Breda Bottling 260k fewer, 121k more in all, and Puurs Drinks Co-packing (BE) fills 59k cases. While it is down, Oss Foods makes 39k more cases than usual, and stock runs €202k higher on average. Service stays at 99.50% (baseline 99.50%). The year costs €242k more than the baseline.

takeaways.title: A supplier goes dark
takeaways.action: It saw the shutdown coming and bought 6,965 L of lemon flavour concentrate in the week before it (it would normally buy 0 L), bought 0 L while the vendor was shut, and carried on afterwards.
assumptions: Vendor shut: day 7 to day 98 of the year.
Found out late: the baseline is kept until day 7, then re-planned as an emergency, the best re-plan possible.
Every plan is proven within ±€113,622 of the best possible; a difference inside that is too small to measure.
Prices, costs and the rest of the year's demand are the baseline's.
takeaways.message: Acting ahead wins back €5.35M, 100% of the €5.35M hit.
takeaways.case: Found out on day 7, a supplier goes dark costs €5.35M of profit and service falls to 76.15%. Acting ahead wins back €5.35M, 100% of the €5.35M hit.
calc: Profit a year: baseline €25,202,920; found out on day 7 €19,852,383; acted ahead €25,205,440.
Hit of finding out late = baseline − found out late = €25,202,920 − €19,852,383 = €5,350,536.
Won back by acting ahead = acted ahead − found out late = €25,205,440 − €19,852,383 = €5,353,057.
Share won back = €5,353,057 ÷ €5,350,536 = 100.0%: the €2,521 over is inside the ±€113,622, so the page says all of it.
Read against the ±€113,622 the plans are proven to: a finding.
Orders served, by value: baseline 99.50%, found out late 76.15%, acted ahead 99.50%.
ahead_costs: Against finding out late, acting ahead brings in revenue +€10.68M and spends: raw materials and packaging +€4.20M; production +€665k; warehousing −€4,814; capital tied up in stock +€8,054; transport, toll included +€421k; carbon price +€28k; stock left at year end −€12k. Net on profit: +€5.35M.
Average stock carried (working capital): €537k found out late, €604k acting ahead, €67k more; the capital tied up in it costs €8,054 more a year.
Room to store it: the racking acting ahead fills most is DC Tilburg ambient, at 94% of its 2,100 pallets at its peak against 60% found out late; no racking becomes full.
